text: Back inside, Carrie returns to the placement packet. She explains that DTI needs an executed acknowledgement before the placement can be finalized; Bjorn distinguishes the terms they actually negotiated from a written mark he cannot verify.

Carrie tries the obvious modern workaround—signing by copying a name—but Bjorn rejects imitation as false witness. Gunnar, watching the packet like a piece of equipment, asks what DTI actually requires the mark to prove.

DTI calls before Carrie can solve the signature problem. The floor supervisor explains that the placement cannot be finalized without an executed acknowledgement. Carrie argues from the household's actual compliance, but procedure still requires a valid mark.
Bjorn challenges the idea of rent as tribute; Carrie lists what the household owes, and Gunnar turns the lease into a simple two-sided ledger of tenant and building obligations.

The issue ends with the studio visibly transformed from temporary placement into a household: the key, map, packet, bedding, contained heat and shared routines now belong to one coherent space. Bjorn names the home as theirs under law, while Carrie—outside the locked door—allows herself one private line before leaving.
One sign reads DEPARTMENT OF TEMPORAL INTEGRATION.
Bjorn turns the book so Gunnar can see.
